title: Chapter 9. Vasu Ghosha: the Lord's Bhavas, Separation, Nityananda, Prayers
html:
Padas of Vasu (Vasudeva) Ghosha known from the Padakalpataru (PK), in the order of the lilas: Gaura in the kirtana of Navadvipa, His form, His rest and the boat play on the Ganga; the Lord in Krishna's mood and in the mood of Radha pining in separation (gaura-chandrikas to the sections of PK on impending and accomplished separation); the devotees' longing for Gaura who has gone; praise of Nityananda; stavas and prarthanas — prayers to Gauranga. Majumdar regards Vasu Ghosha as an eyewitness of the Navadvipa kirtanas and counts these padas among his padas on the Lord's bhava, on Nityananda and among his stavas. The text follows PK, checked against the scans, with the manuscript variants from PK's apparatus, the Gaura-pada-tarangini (GPT1 — 1st ed., 1903; GPT2 — 2nd ed., 1934) and the Kshanada-gita-chintamani (KGC); the Bengali original, variants and word-for-word translation are in the full version of the book.

1. Vasu Ghosha — "nabadvīpe udaya karilā dvija-rāja…" (PK 1494)

Gaura in the kirtana of Navadvipa: the moon risen in the darkness of Kali among the stars, His companions; grey with dust, He sways on the waves of bhava, sings "Hari, Hari" and stands still in the tribhanga pose; at His left is Gadadhara; remembering Vrindavana, the Lord weeps and pours a downpour of the holy name upon the world. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "the spring rasa." Raga dhanashi or vasanta.1

নবদ্বীপে উদয় করিলা দ্বিজ-রাজ ।
কলি-তিমির ঘোর গোরাচাঁদে উজোর
পারিষদ-তারাগণ মাঝ ॥ ধ্রু ॥

nabadvīpe udaya karilā dvija-rāja |
kali-timira ghora gorācām̐de ujora
pāriṣada-tārāgaṇa mājha || dhru ||

nabadvīpe — in Navadvipa; udaya karilā — has risen; dvija-rāja — the king of the twice-born (the moon; the best of brahmanas); kali-timira ghora — the darkness of Kali is dense; gorācām̐de ujora — lit up by Gorachand (Gorachand shines); pāriṣada-tārā-gaṇa — the stars, His companions; mājha — amid

1.1(Refrain) In Navadvipa the king of the twice-born has risen2 —
dense is the darkness of Kali, but Gorachand shines
amid the stars — His companions.

কীর্ত্তনে ঢর ঢর অঙ্গ ধূলি-ধূসর
হালত ভাব-তরঙ্গে ।
করে করতাল ধরি বোলত হরি হরি
খেণে খেণে রহই ত্রিভঙ্গে ॥

kīrttane ḍhara ḍhara aṅga dhūli-dhūsara
hālata bhāba-taraṅge |
kare karatāla dhari bolata hari hari
kheṇe kheṇe rahai tribhaṅge ||

kīrttane — in kirtana; ḍhara ḍhara — brimming over (with love); aṅga — body; dhūli-dhūsara — grey with dust; hālata — sways; bhāba-taraṅge — on the waves of bhava; kare — in His hands; karatāla dhari — holding karatalas; bolata hari hari — says (sings) "Hari, Hari"; khene khene — again and again; rahai tribhaṅge — stands bent in three places

1.2In kirtana, brimming over with love, grey all over with dust,
He sways on the waves of bhava;
karatalas in His hands, He sings, "Hari, Hari!" —
and again and again stands still, bent in three places.3

বামে প্রিয় গদাধর কান্ধের উপরে তার
সুবলিত বাহু আজানে ।
সোঙরি বৃন্দাবন আকুল অনুখণ
ধারা বহে অরুণ-নয়ানে ॥

bāme priya gadādhara kāndhera upare tāra
subalita bāhu ājāne |
soṅari bṛndābana ākula anukhaṇa
dhārā bahe aruṇa-nayāne ||

bāme — at the left; priya gadādhara — dear Gadadhara; kāndhera upare tāra — on his shoulder; subalita bāhu — the graceful (rounded) arm; ājāne — reaching to the knees; soṅari bṛndābana — remembering Vrindavana; ākula anukhaṇa — ceaselessly yearning; dhārā bahe — streams flow; aruṇa-nayāne — from the reddish eyes

1.3At His left is dear Gadadhara,
and on his shoulder rests the Lord's graceful arm that reaches to the knees.4
Remembering Vrindavana, ceaselessly yearning,
He sheds streams of tears from His reddish eyes.

আঁখিযুগ ঝর ঝর যেন নব জলধর
দশন বিজুরী জিনি ছটা ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষ গীতে কলি-জীব উদ্ধারিতে
বরিখল হরি-নাম-ঘটা ॥

ām̐khiyuga jhara jhara yena naba jaladhara
daśana bijurī jini chaṭā |
bāsudeba ghoṣa gīte kali-jība uddhārite
barikhala hari-nāma-ghaṭā ||

ām̐khi-yuga — both eyes; jhara jhara — pour and pour; yena naba jaladhara — like a fresh raincloud; daśana — teeth; bijurī jini chaṭā — their radiance outshines lightning; bāsudeba ghoṣa gīte — in Vasudeva Ghosha's song (Vasudeva Ghosha sings); kali-jība uddhārite — to deliver the souls of Kali; barikhala — has rained; hari-nāma-ghaṭā — a downpour (profusion) of Hari's name

1.4His eyes pour and pour like a fresh raincloud,
His teeth shine brighter than lightning.
Vasudeva Ghosha sings: to deliver the souls of the age of Kali,
He has rained a downpour of Hari's name.5

MS P-R-Sa no. 2044. GPT1 — p. 131, no. 59 (raga dhanashi). Majumdar counts PK 1494 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's
bhava.

spontaneously assumes Krishna's form.

2. Vasu Ghosha — "cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare…" (PK 973)

Gaura's form in Nadia: "Come, let us go and see Gora!" — His body brighter than tested gold, His arms reaching to the knees like golden pillars, a red cloth at His waist, a garland of malati down to His feet; the poet is ready to give his life for Him. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "anuraga: setting out to the tryst by night." Raga suhai.6

চল দেখি গিয়া গোরা অতি মনোহরে ।
অপরূপ রূপ গোরা নদীয়া নগরে ॥

cala dekhi giyā gorā ati manohare |
aparūpa rūpa gorā nadīyā nagare ||

cala dekhi giyā — come, let us go and see; gorā — Gora; ati manohare — exceedingly beautiful; aparūpa rūpa — the wondrous form; gorā — of Gora; nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia

2.1Come, let us go and see Gora, beautiful beyond words:
wondrous is Gora's form in the town of Nadia!

ঢল ঢল কষিল কাঞ্চন জিনি অঙ্গ ।
কে দেখি ধৈরজ ধরে নয়ান-তরঙ্গ ॥

ḍhala ḍhala kaṣila kāñcana jini aṅga |
ke dekhi dhairaja dhare nayāna-taraṅga ||

ḍhala ḍhala — tender, radiant (shimmering); kaṣila kāñcana — tested gold (tried on the touchstone); jini — surpassing; aṅga — body; ke dekhi — who, seeing; dhairaja dhare — keeps composure; nayāna-taraṅga — the waves of the eyes

2.2His body, tender and radiant, outshines tested gold;
who, seeing the waves of His eyes, can keep his composure?

আজানুলম্বিত ভুজ কনকের স্তম্ভ ।
অরুণ বসন কটি বিপুল নিতম্ব ॥

ājānulambita bhuja kanakera stambha |
aruṇa basana kaṭi bipula nitamba ||

ājānu-lambita — reaching down to the knees; bhuja — arms; kanakera stambha — golden pillars; aruṇa basana — red cloth; kaṭi — at the waist; bipula nitamba — broad hips

2.3His arms reach to His knees like golden pillars,
a red cloth is at His waist, broad are His hips.7

মালতীর মালা গলে আপাদ দোলনি ।
বাসু কহে চল দিব পরাণ নিছনি ॥

mālatīra mālā gale āpāda dolani |
bāsu kahe cala diba parāṇa nichani ||

mālatīra mālā — a garland of malati; gale — on the neck; āpāda dolani — swaying down to the feet; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; cala — come; diba parāṇa nichani — I will give my life as nichhani (as an offering waved around Him)

2.4A garland of malati sways on His neck down to His feet.
Says Vasu: "Come — I will give my life for Him!"8

abhisārānurāgaḥ rātrau yathā । śrīgauracandraḥ," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৯৭৩॥"); raga suhai; MS P-R-Sa no. 1423. The same pada stands in PK a second time — PK 2176 (vol. 3, PDF pp. 259–260, printed pp. 248–249; 19th pallava, no. 9; MS P-R-Sa no. 2284), in the section of padas spoken by the women of Nadia, with the ending "Says Vasu: 'I will go and offer [Him] my youth'"; so too in GPT1 (p. 161, no. 15, raga shri), among padas in nagari-bhava. Majumdar counts PK 973 among the padas on the Lord's form and PK 2176 under nagari-bhava. The PK 973 recension is translated here; the 2176 recension belongs to nagari-bhava: worship of Gaura in the spirit of "Gaura-nagari" is not accepted by the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta). samudrika-shastra; so too Vrindavana Dasa and Krishnadasa Kaviraja describe the Lord's form. person to ward off misfortune and then given away; here the poet gives his very life.

3. Vasu Ghosha — "śutiyāche gorācām̐da śayana-mandire…" (PK 656)

Gorachand lies in His bedchamber on a wondrous couch, languid; it is as if the Creator had strained lightning from the clouds and put all rasa into Him; Vasudeva Ghosha looks on in joy. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "languor after the play" (rasalasa). Raga vibhasa.9

শুতিয়াছে গোরাচাঁদ শয়ন-মন্দিরে ।
বিচিত্র পালঙ্ক শেজ অতি মনোহরে ॥

śutiyāche gorācām̐da śayana-mandire |
bicitra pālaṅka śeja ati manohare ||

śutiyāche — lies (asleep); gorācām̐da — Gorachand; śayana-mandire — in the bedchamber; bicitra pālaṅka — on a wondrous couch; śeja — bed; ati manohare — very lovely

3.1Gorachand lies in His bedchamber
on a wondrous couch, on a lovely bed.

আলসে অবশ-তনু গোরা নটরায় ।
কি কহব অঙ্গ-শোভা কহনে না যায় ॥

ālase abaśa-tanu gorā naṭarāya |
ki kahaba aṅga-śobhā kahane nā yāya ||

ālase — from languor; abaśa-tanu — His body limp; gorā naṭarāya — Gora, the king of dancers; ki kahaba — what shall I say; aṅga-śobhā — the beauty of His body; kahane nā yāya — cannot be told

3.2Languid is the body of Gora, the king of dancers —
how can I tell the beauty of His body? It cannot be told!10

মেঘের বিজুরী কিবা ছানিয়া যতনে ।
কত রস দিয়া বিধি কৈল নিরমাণে ॥

meghera bijurī kibā chāniyā yatane |
kata rasa diyā bidhi kaila niramāṇe ||

meghera bijurī — the lightning of the clouds; kibā — as if; chāniyā yatane — straining (kneading) it with care; kata rasa diyā — putting in so much rasa; bidhi — the Creator; kaila niramāṇe — fashioned (Him)

3.3As if lightning had been carefully strained from the clouds —
so much rasa did the Creator put in, fashioning Him!

অতি মনোহর শেজ বিচিত্র বালিশে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে দেখে মনের হরিষে ॥

ati manohara śeja bicitra bāliśe |
bāsudeba ghoṣe dekhe manera hariṣe ||

ati manohara śeja — a most lovely bed; bicitra bāliśe — with wondrous pillows; bāsudeba ghoṣe — Vasudeva Ghosha; dekhe — looks on; manera hariṣe — with joy in his heart

3.4A lovely bed, wondrous pillows —
Vasudeva Ghosha looks on with joy in his heart.

no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৬৫৬॥"); raga vibhasa; MS P-R-Sa no. 1131. GPT1 — pp. 361–362, no. 53 (raga vibhasa). According to PK's index of first lines (vol. 5), the same pada stands in PK a second time — PK 2474 (vol. 4, the section on the night and morning plays); in the scan of vol. 4 (IA 354459) the leaf with PK 2474–2478 is missing between PDF pp. 44 and 45, so its variants have not been checked. The catalogue wrongly linked PK 656 to the GPT pada "nācata śacītanaya gaurasundara…" (VG-057). Majumdar counts PK 656 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. PK's section "rasalasa" is about the languor of Radha and Krishna after the night's play; the gaura-chandrika shows the Lord wearied by the night's kirtana and bhava. "gh": "in languor" (alase) instead of "languid" (ālase; GPT1 — "ābeśe," with "ālase" in a note); P-R-Sa: "how can I tell the beauty of His body" (ki kaba aṅgera śobhā), "says Vasudeva Ghosha" (kaya) instead of "looks on" (dekhe).

4. Vasu Ghosha — "nā jāniye gorācām̐dera kona bhāba mane…" (PK 1409)

The boat play on the Ganga: Gorachand goes to the bank with His companions, steps into a boat with Gadadhara and steers it Himself; everyone cries "We are sinking!" and bails out water, and, remembering the former play, floats in the waters of prema, while the Lord, looking at Gadadhara, gently smiles. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "the boat play" (nauka-vilasa). Raga tudi.11

না জানিয়ে গোরাচাঁদের কোন ভাব মনে ।
সুরধুনী-তীরে গেলা সহচর সনে ॥

nā jāniye gorācām̐dera kona bhāba mane |
suradhunī-tīre gelā sahacara sane ||

nā jāniye — I do not know; gorācām̐dera — of Gorachand; kona bhāba mane — what bhava in the heart; suradhunī-tīre — to the bank of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); gelā — went; sahacara sane — with His companions

4.1I do not know what bhava is in Gorachand's heart:
He went with His companions to the bank of the Suradhuni.12

প্রিয় গদাধর আদি সঙ্গে ত করিয়া ।
নৌকায় চড়িলা গৌর প্রেমাবেশ হৈয়া ॥

priya gadādhara ādi saṅge ta kariyā |
naukāya caṛilā gaura premābeśa haiyā ||

priya gadādhara ādi — dear Gadadhara and others; saṅge ta kariyā — taking with Him; naukāya caṛilā — stepped into a boat; gaura — Gaura; premābeśa haiyā — overwhelmed by prema

4.2Taking with Him dear Gadadhara and others,
Gaura stepped into a boat, overwhelmed by prema.

আপনে কাণ্ডারী হৈয়া বায় নৌকাখানি ।
ডুবিল ডুবিল বলি সিঞ্চে সভে পানি ॥

āpane kāṇḍārī haiyā bāya naukākhāni |
ḍubila ḍubila bali siñce sabhe pāni ||

āpane — Himself; kāṇḍārī haiyā — becoming the helmsman; bāya naukākhāni — steers the boat; ḍubila ḍubila bali — crying "we are sinking, sinking"; siñce — bail out (splash); sabhe — all; pāni — water

4.3Becoming the helmsman Himself, He steers the boat;
"We are sinking, sinking!" all cry, and bail out the water.

পারিষদগণ সবে হরি হরি বোলে ।
পুরব সোঙরি কেহো ভাসে প্রেম-জলে ॥

pāriṣadagaṇa sabe hari hari bole |
puraba soṅari keho bhāse prema-jale ||

pāriṣada-gaṇa sabe — all the companions; hari hari bole — call out "Hari, Hari"; puraba soṅari — remembering the former (play); keho — some; bhāse — float; prema-jale — in the waters of prema

4.4All the companions call out, "Hari, Hari!" —
remembering the former play, some float in the waters of prema.13

গদাধর-মুখ হেরি মৃদু মৃদু হাসে ।
বাসুদেব ঘোষে কহে মনের উল্লাসে ॥

gadādhara-mukha heri mṛdu mṛdu hāse |
bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe manera ullāse ||

gadādhara-mukha heri — looking into Gadadhara's face; mṛdu mṛdu hāse — smiles ever so gently; bāsudeba ghoṣe kahe — says Vasudeva Ghosha; manera ullāse — with jubilation in his heart

4.5Looking into Gadadhara's face, He smiles ever so gently —
so says Vasudeva Ghosha, with jubilation in his heart.

naukā-bilāsa । taducita śrīmahāprabhu," no. 1 (mark "॥১॥১৪০৯॥"); raga tudi; MS P-R-Sa no. 1925. GPT1 — p. 333, no. 38 (raga tudi; among the padas on the dana-lila). Majumdar counts PK 1409 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Compare Ramananda's pada on the same play (PK 1417, chapter 6). the helm is Krishna, Gadadhara is Radha. MSS "k," "c," P-R-Sa: "Himself" — āpani (the same); P-R-Sa: "guides" (bahe) instead of "steers" (bāya), "with joy" (hariṣe) instead of "with jubilation" (ullāse). GPT1: "smiles to Himself" (mane mane hāse).

5. Vasu Ghosha — "āre mora gorā dvijamaṇi…" (PK 54)

The Lord in the mood of Krishna stricken with purvaraga: "Radha, Radha!" Gora calls, weeps and rolls on the ground, chants Radha's name with great devotion, rivers of tears flow from His eyes, and again and again He loses consciousness. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika to the section "Sri Krishna's purvaraga." Raga suhai, tala jayajayanti.14

আরে মোর গোরা দ্বিজমণি ।
রাধা রাধা বলি কান্দে লোটায় ধরণী ॥

āre mora gorā dvijamaṇi |
rādhā rādhā bali kānde loṭāya dharaṇī ||

āre mora — O my; gorā — Gora; dvijamaṇi — jewel of the twice-born (brahmanas); rādhā rādhā bali — saying "Radha, Radha"; kānde — weeps; loṭāya dharaṇī — rolls on the ground

5.1O my Gora, jewel of the twice-born!
"Radha, Radha!" He calls, weeps and rolls on the ground.

রাধা নাম জপে গোরা পরম যতনে ।
সুরধুনী-ধারা বহে অরুণ নয়ানে ॥

rādhā nāma jape gorā parama yatane |
suradhunī-dhārā bahe aruṇa nayāne ||

rādhā nāma jape — chants Radha's name; gorā — Gora; parama yatane — with great devotion; suradhunī-dhārā — streams of the Suradhuni (the Ganga); bahe — flow; aruṇa nayāne — from the reddish eyes

5.2Gora chants Radha's name with great devotion,
and streams of the Suradhuni flow from His reddish eyes.15

খেনে খেনে গোরা-অঙ্গ ভূমে গড়ি যায় ।
রাধা নাম বলি খেনে খেনে মুরুছায় ॥

khene khene gorā-aṅga bhūme gaṛi yāya |
rādhā nāma bali khene khene muruchāya ||

khene khene — again and again; gorā-aṅga — Gora's body; bhūme gaṛi yāya — rolls on the ground; rādhā nāma bali — uttering Radha's name; muruchāya — swoons

5.3Again and again Gora's body rolls on the ground,
again and again, uttering Radha's name, He swoons.

পুলকে পূরল তনু গদগদ বোল ।
বাসু কহে গোরা কেন এত উতরোল ॥

pulake pūrala tanu gadagada bola |
bāsu kahe gorā kena eta utarola ||

pulake pūrala tanu — the body is filled with gooseflesh (pulaka); gadagada bola — faltering speech; bāsu kahe — says Vasu; gorā kena — why is Gora; eta utarola — so agitated

5.4His body is thrilled with gooseflesh, His voice falters.
Says Vasu: "Why is Gora so agitated?"

no. 1 (mark "॥১॥৫৪॥"); "suhai । jayajayantī." GPT1 — p. 297, no. 16 (jayajayanti). Majumdar counts PK 54 among Vasu's padas on the Lord's bhava. Usually the Lord abides in Radha's mood, but His companions also saw His mood of Krishna longing for the gopis (cf. CC Adi 17: the Lord chants "Gopi, gopi!"). repeated by Radhamohana Dasa in his pada on Gaura and Gauridasa (GPT1, p. 290, no. 43).

6. Vasu Ghosha — "sakala bhakata meli ānande hulāhuli…" (PK 2041)

In the morning the devotees come with joyful cries to see Gauranga, but He has not slept all night and His face is wan; rising, He sits down again on the ground, alone, apart; the devotees are alarmed, not understanding what bhava has risen in His heart; one washes His face, another tidies His hair. In PK it is the gaura-chandrika "on the next day" to the section "recollections of the complete union." Raga pahida.16
